title: The Consultant Who Planted Bombs Then Sold Security Contracts
hook: A security consultant was found to be planting explosive devices at factories, then offering his services to 'investigate' the blasts.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme betrayal of trust plus violent crime creates massive outrage and shock value.

title: How a Meat Company Sold 'Beef' That Was Horse and Rat DNA
hook: For years, a major supplier sold '100% beef' burgers that contained horse, rat, and even human DNA fragments.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out factor plus universal fear of unknowingly eating contaminated food drives shares.

title: The Start-up That Sold AI on a Chip—It Was Just a Guy in a Server Room
hook: A hot AI hardware startup raised millions for a revolutionary chip, but the 'AI' was actually a human typing responses from a closet.
why_this_can_go_viral: The bait-and-switch of 'AI' secretly being human triggers both laughter and anger at Silicon Valley hype.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Parking Meters—Then Made Waiting a Subscription
hook: A single company bought the parking rights in dozens of cities, then introduced a subscription fee just to park in front of your own home.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone hates parking fees; a subscription model on top feels like dystopian greed.

title: The Ad That Used Your Typing Speed to Detect Anxiety—Then Sold You Drugs
hook: An online ad analyzed how fast you typed to determine your stress level, then served you prescription medication ads before you even felt sick.
why_this_can_go_viral: Creepy, real-time psychological tracking feels like Black Mirror, sparking privacy outrage.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Cochlear Implant Patents—Then Made Silence a Premium
hook: A hearing aid company bought every cochlear implant patent, then stopped improving tech and charged deaf people monthly fees just to hear.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploiting a vulnerable disability for profit triggers maximum empathy and outrage.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI Recruiters'—They Were Ex-Convicts in a Call Center
hook: A hiring platform claimed AI was screening candidates—actually it was a room of felons reading scripts, using fake accents to seem 'neutral'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Irony of criminals deciding who gets hired; plus the AI lie feels like a betrayal.

title: The Ad That Detected Your Cough Through the Mic—Then Sold You Cold Medicine
hook: An audio ad on your phone used the microphone to listen for coughs, then instantly served a cold remedy coupon before you even typed a symptom.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that your phone listens for illness is deeply unsettling and highly shareable.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of 'Hypoallergenic' Skincare That Caused Chemical Burns
hook: A luxury skincare brand sold 'hypoallergenic' creams that were actually made with industrial acid, burning thousands of customers—then buried the lawsuits.
why_this_can_go_viral: Physical harm from a beauty product creates visceral fear and anger; plus the cover-up adds conspiracy layers.

title: The Trader Who Used a Drone to Drop a Fake 'Emergency Landing' Sound on a Factory
hook: A short seller flew a drone over a rival's facility playing a recorded emergency siren, causing a panic that halted production and crashed the stock.
why_this_can_go_viral: Weaponizing a drone with sound in a high-stakes financial heist is cinematic and new.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Cloud Storage—Then Held Your Photos for Ransom
hook: A single cloud storage company bought every competitor in a region, then shut down free tiers and demanded payment to unlock people's lifelong photo archives.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone has digital memories at risk; the idea of paying to access your own photos feels like extortion.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Wi-Fi Router Design by Replacing a Factory's Workers with His Own
hook: A corporate spy convinced a factory to hire his 'temp agency'—then replaced the entire assembly line with his own engineers who copied the blueprints.
why_this_can_go_viral: A long-con with high stakes; viewers love the audacity of replacing an entire workforce.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI Fortune Tellers' for Stock Tips—They Were Retired Gamblers
hook: A startup claimed its AI predicted stock movements using 'machine learning'—actually it was old casino dealers using gut instinct and a random number generator.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mixing gambling superstition with tech hype creates a hilarious yet dark exposé.

title: The Ad That Detected Your Loneliness from Midnight Scrolling—Then Sold You Dating Apps
hook: An ad network analyzed your phone usage after midnight to infer loneliness, then targeted you with dating app ads designed to exploit vulnerability.
why_this_can_go_viral: Targeting emotional low points feels predatory and deeply relatable, especially for night owls.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of 'Non-Toxic' Furniture That Off-Gassed Cyanide
hook: A furniture chain sold 'eco-friendly' sofas that actually released low levels of cyanide gas from flame retardants—they hid test results for decades.
why_this_can_go_viral: Poison in your living room is a terrifying, relatable violation of home safety.

title: The Trader Who Faked a 'CEO Kidnapping' Voicemail to Sell the Stock Short
hook: A hedge fund manager left a fake voicemail that sounded like a CEO being kidnapped, then shorted the stock before the market could verify the hoax.
why_this_can_go_viral: High drama, criminal creativity, and a scheme so brazen it feels like a movie plot.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Key Nutrients—Then Made Supplements a Forced Subscription
hook: A vitamin company bought the global supply of a critical nutrient used in baby formula, then only sold it via expensive, hard-to-cancel subscriptions.
why_this_can_go_viral: Profiting off babies' health is a guaranteed outrage trigger; plus subscription traps are universally hated.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Car Engine Blueprint by Replacing the Factory's Blueprint Paper
hook: A corporate spy swapped out the factory's official blueprint paper with a heat-reactive copy that turned invisible after being read, then photographed the originals.
why_this_can_go_viral: Clever, almost magical low-tech spy trick; viewers will be fascinated by the disappearing ink method.
